newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
RAO DENIED BAIL IN FORGERY CASE

Former prime minister Narasimha Rao was denied bail in the St Kitts forgery case. He was asked to surrender on or before November 14, 1996. The chief metropolitan magistrate also rejected a bail plea by a former minister, K.K. Tewary. Rao later appealed to the Delhi High Court. His plea is expected to be heard on Wednesday, sources said. Warrants were also issued to two other co-accused in the forgery case, Chandraswami and his secretary K N Aggarwal. The latter are in jail in connection with the $100,000 Lakhubhai Pathak cheating case. Rao will appear as an accused in the cheating case before the special judge on Wednesday.
The Hindustan Times
FORMER MINISTER RETURNS TO CONGRESS

Former minister Madhavrao Singh Scindia returned to the Congress fold at the request of party chief Sitaram Kesri. Scindia's return marked first step towards the coming together of estranged party leaders. The Congress move jolted the United Front, of which Scindia's Madhya Pradesh Vikash Party was a part. Scindhia had won the Gwalior seat in the last parliamentary polls in April and May as an independent.
The Economic Times
GDP GROWTH RATE LIKELY TO BE 6.5 PCT

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said a gross domestic product growth rate of around 6.5 percent was expected in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). The Reserve Bank of India, Planning Commission and the chief economic adviser agreed on the projected figure. Finance ministry officials said the current year's budgeted disinvestment target was unlikely to be met. Referring to an economic growth rate of 6.5 percent or so expected this year, Chidambaram said growth was also limited by the level of other financial parameters.
FOREIGN FIRMS MAY BE BROUGHT IN FOR BOMBAY HIGH REVAMP

The Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) is likely to bring in multinationals (MNCs) for rehabilitation of Bombay High field. This could be in the form of a fee for a consultancy and a risk-sharing arrangement with a percentage payment related to increase in production. Earlier talks on production sharing for the Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) programme of Bombay High had failed. The firms had then quoted a figure of a 40-60 million tonnes rise in production over 15-20 years at a cost of $1.5 billion. Current talks are with firms such as Total, Arco and Chevron for the EOR programme. Meanwhile, ONGC plans to start the first phase of rehabilitation of Bombay High (North) at a cost of 15 billion rupees.
GOVERNMENT LOOKING TO SHORE UP OIL POOL ACCOUNT

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said the government was examining options to contain the Oil Industry Pool Account deficit, estimated at 138 billion rupees at end-March. He agreed with the oil ministry's contention that the oil import bill could end up around $9 billion in the fiscal year ending next March, against a budgeted estimate of $7.59 billion. But the minister said this was unlikely to have an adverse impact on the balance of payments position. The government earlier had sharply raised prices when the deficit was estimated at 117 billion rupees by end-year.
Financial Express
LIMIT ON COMMERCIAL PAPER RAISED TO 100 PCT

Issuance of commercial papers (CP) by corporates can go up to 100 percent of their eligible working capital limits, the central bank (RBI) said. But, the CPs first will have to be adjusted against the cash credit component of the overall working capital. On credit policy, RBI had reduced the cash-credit component to 25 percent from an earlier 40 percent for companies with maximum permissible bank finance (MPBF) of over 200 million rupees. Following reductions in the cash-credit limits the base for issuance of CPs grew narrower. In view of this, the credit policy delinked the issuance of CPs from the cash-credit limit.
AMPHETRONIX STAKE HIKE APPROVED

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) has allowed Amphenoi Corporation of the U.S. to hike its stake in Amphetronix Ltd and make it a 100 percent owned arm. The FIPB decision cleared the way for the Murugappa group to divest its holding in Amphetronix. Amphetronix manufactures connectors and cable assemblies with applications in the telecom, industrial, defence and space sectors in the domestic market.
MAHARASHTRA PLANS 4000 MW HYDEL CAPACITY

The Maharashtra government has fixed a target to create 40,000 mw hydroelectric power generation capacity by 2000-01. Major among the projects being undertaken by the state is the Krishna Valley project. The project, estimated to cost 100,6 billion rupees, will incorporate several minor hydroelectric power projects to generate 224 mw of electricity. A 1,000 mw hydel project at Koyna is being set up with technical help from Cegelec of France. The 400 mw hydel project in Amravati district is awaiting clearance.
SCHEMES FLOATED TO ATTRACT INVESTMENT IN ELECTRONICS

The government has floated two schemes to attract foreign direct investment in the electronic software and hardware sectors. They include the software Technology Park (STP) and the Electronic Hardware Technology Park (EHTP). Licensing has been abolished in this sector to woo foreign investors. The 100 percent export-oriented STP scheme allows 100 percent foreign equity, duty free imports and the re-export of capital goods. The EHTP scheme allows foreign equity up to 100 percent, duty-free imports of raw material, components and capital goods, and a tax holiday for five years.
Business Standard
13 CONSORTIA IN RACE FOR GUJARAT POWER PLANT

Gujarat has shortlisted 14 consortia to set up a 615 mw 24 billion rupee gas-based power plant. They include Torrent group along with Siemens and Power Gen, Gujarat Gas and Eastern Generation, Essar with Hanjing of South Korea, and Larson and Toubro with Mirubeni of Japan. Those bidding individually are UK's British Gas, Addition Mission and International Generation Company, Reliance Power, Amoco and Coastal Power of US, Tata Electric and China Light of Hong Kong. Reliance is bidding for most of the proposed 20 small power projects.
LOAN COMPONENT ROLLOVER TO BE REVIEWED EVERY YEAR

The central bank (RBI) has advised a strict annual review of the loan component to prevent the present credit delivery system from degenerating into the earlier cash credit system. The RBI demanded regular annual review of the working capital limit and said the credit limit should not be allowed to continue without such a review. The apex bank plans to allow lead banks in consortium to bifurcate a loan between the cash credit component and the loan component. This will be subject to the overall limit of the borrower being bifurcated.
